target: Distinct A-band styles in both modes, typical competitive Arena games ten-plus turns per player; proposed working band 10-14, not a hard minimum or a measured result. Campaign XVII-XX difficult but beatable.

starters.rationale: Reserves and straightforward defense/attacks provide a reliable opening.
Improved Drone and Pulse Pistol help; large-machine setup is still resource hungry.
Pack damage and blood resources are productive early.
Efficient suit/cycling pool gives broad early flexibility; pool parity unresolved.
Recurring Dagger and efficient Skills provide consistent damage.
Two starting totems offer immediate value before row investment.
Stance sequencing is strong but mistakes can expose the hero.
Starting Spell Power supplies an early spend/rebuild rhythm.
Small Thralls and slower Fate/Consume development need protection.
Gun and drink setup can compete, but HP/Hangover management is less forgiving.

basis: Static rule/card review and explicit conditional arithmetic, not simulation. Zero measured matches. One second-hand Golemancer 160-HP campaign observation has no deck, replay, tier or turn count. Overall grades consider access/disruption; long grades assume a functioning engine survives to turns 10-15. Existing opening/turns 6-10 and Campaign grades are carried forward unless a named correction says otherwise.
status: Local review; only the 15-to-20-minute Arena clock is implemented. Balance proposals are not applied.
source: 9f16335 plus local decision #600 timer change; combat/content match released rules 79. Decision #601 records this review.

ratings.name: Paladin
ratings.scaling: Retention supports defense and Barrier attacks, but constant Barrier generation converges rather than growing forever. More turns help only if the deck increases its generation or converts it into a finish.
ratings.rationale: Retention supports defense and Barrier attacks, but constant Barrier generation converges rather than growing forever. More turns help only if the deck increases its generation or converts it into a finish.
ratings.watch: Timeout/sustain risk; piercing and direct HP loss bypass the main defense.
ratings.pacing: Timeout/sustain risk; piercing and direct HP loss bypass the main defense.

ratings.name: Marshal
ratings.scaling: Four Reserves and up to 40% Attack bonus provide strong repeatable turns, not permanent turn-by-turn scaling. The pool must supply Might, Exposed and finishers to compete with growing engines.
ratings.rationale: Four Reserves and up to 40% Attack bonus provide strong repeatable turns, not permanent turn-by-turn scaling. The pool must supply Might, Exposed and finishers to compete with growing engines.
ratings.watch: Watch damage after turn ten and resource access after consuming the initial accelerants.
ratings.pacing: Watch damage after turn ten and resource access after consuming the initial accelerants.

ratings.name: Blood Knight
ratings.scaling: First paid HP card helps charge Retaliation despite Arena HP dilution. Stored 60% and 30 percentage points per owner-round are bounded; multi-hit attacks and resource cards determine the actual ceiling.
ratings.rationale: First paid HP card helps charge Retaliation despite Arena HP dilution. Stored 60% and 30 percentage points per owner-round are bounded; multi-hit attacks and resource cards determine the actual ceiling.
ratings.watch: Cheap HP payments are much safer at 480+ HP; resource burst can finish before the target band.
ratings.pacing: Cheap HP payments are much safer at 480+ HP; resource burst can finish before the target band.

ratings.name: Swarmwright
ratings.build: Many small summons / continuous attack bonuses
ratings.scaling: Four slots and retained Fabrication reward replacement summons. One Primed per body is useful but is not the only scaling: every three successful non-starting summons adds damage to every companion hit. Shared HP engines and HP-payoff cards also matter.
ratings.rationale: Four slots and retained Fabrication reward replacement summons. One Primed per body is useful but is not the only scaling: every three successful non-starting summons adds damage to every companion hit. Shared HP engines and HP-payoff cards also matter.
ratings.watch: Removal taxes setup; compare summon count and attacks actually delivered, not four bodies assumed alive.
ratings.pacing: Removal taxes setup; compare summon count and attacks actually delivered, not four bodies assumed alive.

ratings.name: Golemancer
ratings.recovery: True death banks half earned growth, capped 30; next new large build consumes it. Revive is fresh; scrapping instead transfers half current HP through Salvage.
ratings.rareReliance: Uncommon growth engine; common Crankshaft; rare Heavy Hitter/Meltdown improve burst.
ratings.scaling: Correcting the passive-only picture: all companion healing grows max/current HP. Resonant Pulse, Self-Mending, Patch Job and Reinforced Frame accelerate this; Heavy Hitter and Crankshaft convert max HP into hero attacks. At 160 max HP the companion bonus is already capped at +100%, but these cards continue scaling.
ratings.rationale: Correcting the passive-only picture: all companion healing grows max/current HP. Resonant Pulse, Self-Mending, Patch Job and Reinforced Frame accelerate this; Heavy Hitter and Crankshaft convert max HP into hero attacks. At 160 max HP the companion bonus is already capped at +100%, but these cards continue scaling. Campaign IV-X and XVII-XX estimates rise from A- to A because the previous review underweighted healing growth and HP-conversion cards; this is a corrected hypothesis, not proof of clears.
ratings.watch: High HP-conversion burst; a non-Taunt machine can be bypassed. Friend report of easy 160 HP is anecdotal, not a measured match. No automatic buff.
ratings.pacing: High HP-conversion burst; a non-Taunt machine can be bypassed. Friend report of easy 160 HP is anecdotal, not a measured match. No automatic buff.

ratings.name: Artillerist
ratings.scaling: Permanent Might is especially productive on Rotary Cannon and other multi-hit weapons. Weapon Bench and Ion Lance provide additional pool growth; the small first-Attack Barrier does not itself solve survival.
ratings.rationale: Permanent Might is especially productive on Rotary Cannon and other multi-hit weapons. Weapon Bench and Ion Lance provide additional pool growth; the small first-Attack Barrier does not itself solve survival.
ratings.watch: Can race ahead with multi-hit bonuses; check survivability separately from sustained damage.
ratings.pacing: Can race ahead with multi-hit bonuses; check survivability separately from sustained damage.

ratings.name: Beastmaster
ratings.scaling: Sharing 75% Might scales the whole pack and new summons inherit current hero Might. Long games help a functioning Might engine, but protecting or replacing bodies remains a real cost.
ratings.rationale: Sharing 75% Might scales the whole pack and new summons inherit current hero Might. Long games help a functioning Might engine, but protecting or replacing bodies remains a real cost.
ratings.watch: Removal and direct hero pressure prevent equating a full board with guaranteed output.
ratings.pacing: Removal and direct hero pressure prevent equating a full board with guaranteed output.

ratings.name: Reaver
ratings.recovery: Moderate; hero HP is the resource
ratings.scaling: First HP payment draws and primes each turn; this improves consistency rather than providing independent exponential growth. Hunter Might, companions and HP-payment resources supply the late game.
ratings.rationale: First HP payment draws and primes each turn; this improves consistency rather than providing independent exponential growth. Hunter Might, companions and HP-payment resources supply the late game.
ratings.watch: Burst funded by cheap blood resources; first-payment benefit should not be mistaken for every-payment benefit.
ratings.pacing: Burst funded by cheap blood resources; first-payment benefit should not be mistaken for every-payment benefit.

ratings.name: Predator
ratings.scaling: First six additional own-turn draws give two Primed each and later draws give one. This still rewards large draw chains; Hunter blood resources can fund the chain and its payoff.
ratings.rationale: First six additional own-turn draws give two Primed each and later draws give one. This still rewards large draw chains; Hunter blood resources can fund the chain and its payoff.
ratings.watch: High card-throughput burst before turn ten remains possible.
ratings.pacing: High card-throughput burst before turn ten remains possible.

ratings.name: Trapmaster
ratings.recovery: Good if traps can be reset
ratings.scaling: Draw and Barrier depend on opponents triggering traps. Full Trick supplies growing damage for all Trickster Ascendancies; Trapmaster trades some proactive tempo for reactive resource recovery.
ratings.rationale: Draw and Barrier depend on opponents triggering traps. Full Trick supplies growing damage for all Trickster Ascendancies; Trapmaster trades some proactive tempo for reactive resource recovery.
ratings.watch: Opponent control over trap triggers and choice of attack target can reduce reliability.
ratings.pacing: Opponent control over trap triggers and choice of attack target can reduce reliability.

ratings.name: Cardsharp
ratings.scaling: Full Trick gives growing damage/draw and Cardsharp adds one Mana. Cut the Deck cycling improves consistent access; the pool is a large part of the grade, not just the extra Mana.
ratings.rationale: Full Trick gives growing damage/draw and Cardsharp adds one Mana. Cut the Deck cycling improves consistent access; the pool is a large part of the grade, not just the extra Mana.
ratings.watch: Repeatable conditional free draw compresses too many actions into one turn.
ratings.pacing: Repeatable conditional free draw compresses too many actions into one turn.

ratings.name: Seer
ratings.scaling: Keeping the same marked target reaches +50% and Exposed adds pressure. Full Trick and suit cycling continue to develop after Seer itself caps.
ratings.rationale: Keeping the same marked target reaches +50% and Exposed adds pressure. Full Trick and suit cycling continue to develop after Seer itself caps.
ratings.watch: Switching target resets the streak; Taunt and diversions can disrupt the preferred hero focus.
ratings.pacing: Switching target resets the streak; Taunt and diversions can disrupt the preferred hero focus.

ratings.name: Bladedancer
ratings.scaling: Two generated Daggers per turn provide reliable attacks and fuel the Rogue pool. Repeated bonuses and additional hits matter more than the printed Dagger base damage.
ratings.rationale: Two generated Daggers per turn provide reliable attacks and fuel the Rogue pool. Repeated bonuses and additional hits matter more than the printed Dagger base damage.
ratings.watch: Resource/draw chains and repeated amplified attacks can end games early.
ratings.pacing: Resource/draw chains and repeated amplified attacks can end games early.

ratings.name: Bloodletter
ratings.scaling: Extra Bleed/Burn ticks accelerate damage but also decay the stacks again. Sustained reapplication and pool support are necessary; it is not automatically double total damage per stack.
ratings.rationale: Extra Bleed/Burn ticks accelerate damage but also decay the stacks again. Sustained reapplication and pool support are necessary; it is not automatically double total damage per stack.
ratings.watch: Cleanse and application efficiency determine long-fight pressure.
ratings.pacing: Cleanse and application efficiency determine long-fight pressure.

ratings.name: Assassin
ratings.scaling: Skills build up to +60% for the next Attack, with another +20% against a hero at half HP or lower. Sequencing and multi-hit payoffs remain valuable but the passive has bounded amplification.
ratings.rationale: Skills build up to +60% for the next Attack, with another +20% against a hero at half HP or lower. Sequencing and multi-hit payoffs remain valuable but the passive has bounded amplification.
ratings.watch: Execute-window burst rather than unlimited passive growth.
ratings.pacing: Execute-window burst rather than unlimited passive growth.

ratings.name: Totemist
ratings.recovery: Totems are not attackable units; rebuild costs primarily follow own commands/push-outs. Hero pressure still matters.
ratings.scaling: Starting Spirit and qualifying end-turn Spirit grow recurring totem output. The totem row cannot be attacked like companions, so ordinary minion removal is not a counter to this engine.
ratings.rationale: Starting Spirit and qualifying end-turn Spirit grow recurring totem output. The totem row cannot be attacked like companions, so ordinary minion removal is not a counter to this engine.
ratings.watch: Automatic scaling and free recurring sustain can stall or outgrow bounded decks.
ratings.pacing: Automatic scaling and free recurring sustain can stall or outgrow bounded decks.

ratings.name: Spiritwalker
ratings.recovery: Totems are not attackable units; rebuild costs primarily follow own commands/push-outs. Hero pressure still matters.
ratings.scaling: First command/push draw and Barrier give consistency; Spirit Pact can supply additional permanent Spirit. Commands replace or spend the row, whereas opponents do not normally kill its totems.
ratings.rationale: First command/push draw and Barrier give consistency; Spirit Pact can supply additional permanent Spirit. Commands replace or spend the row, whereas opponents do not normally kill its totems.
ratings.watch: Command throughput, stacked Spirit Pact and Storm Sovereign need combined review.
ratings.pacing: Command throughput, stacked Spirit Pact and Storm Sovereign need combined review.

ratings.name: Elementalist
ratings.recovery: Totems are not attackable units; rebuild costs primarily follow own commands/push-outs. Hero pressure still matters.
ratings.scaling: Each element has its own permanent count. First Flame/Frost/Storm each turn grows its payoff, with a switching bonus; mixed-element access supports damage and defense together.
ratings.rationale: Each element has its own permanent count. First Flame/Frost/Storm each turn grows its payoff, with a switching bonus; mixed-element access supports damage and defense together.
ratings.watch: More turns improve all three tracks; grade rises from the old shorter-horizon assessment.
ratings.pacing: More turns improve all three tracks; grade rises from the old shorter-horizon assessment.

ratings.name: Sage
ratings.scaling: Extra Mana on the first Serene exit combines with the base Monk Mana refund. Stance sequencing, recurring Might and Radiant windows give the whole deck scaling beyond the passive refund.
ratings.rationale: Extra Mana on the first Serene exit combines with the base Monk Mana refund. Stance sequencing, recurring Might and Radiant windows give the whole deck scaling beyond the passive refund.
ratings.watch: Large stance turns and 3x Radiant windows can violate the duration target.
ratings.pacing: Large stance turns and 3x Radiant windows can violate the duration target.

ratings.name: Zealot
ratings.build: Controlled Fury / entry and exit growth
ratings.recovery: Good if a safe exit is available
ratings.scaling: First Fury entry each own turn builds toward +40%; first exit Barrier reaches 14. These bonuses cap, while the base class continues gaining Might/Fervor.
ratings.rationale: First Fury entry each own turn builds toward +40%; first exit Barrier reaches 14. These bonuses cap, while the base class continues gaining Might/Fervor.
ratings.watch: Fury incoming-damage exposure is meaningful; do not assume every turn is a safe burst turn.
ratings.pacing: Fury incoming-damage exposure is meaningful; do not assume every turn is a safe burst turn.

ratings.name: Sunwalker
ratings.recovery: Moderate; must reach another Radiant window
ratings.scaling: More Fervor accelerates Radiant and returning up to four Fervor after Radiant improves later access. Morning Prayer copies support continued stance cycles.
ratings.rationale: More Fervor accelerates Radiant and returning up to four Fervor after Radiant improves later access. Morning Prayer copies support continued stance cycles.
ratings.watch: Frequency and size of Radiant lethal windows, including resource acceleration.
ratings.pacing: Frequency and size of Radiant lethal windows, including resource acceleration.

ratings.name: Blademaster
ratings.scaling: Sword Keen and first-Sword draw help consistency. Obsidian Blade scales with retained Power, and Echoing Blade can add hits; a modest-looking passive can sit on a powerful late-game pool.
ratings.rationale: Sword Keen and first-Sword draw help consistency. Obsidian Blade scales with retained Power, and Echoing Blade can add hits; a modest-looking passive can sit on a powerful late-game pool.
ratings.watch: Stacked extra Blade hits and Power growth, not just one Keen per hit.
ratings.pacing: Stacked extra Blade hits and Power growth, not just one Keen per hit.

ratings.name: Archmage
ratings.scaling: Power spending, first-spell amplification and next-turn refund support repeated bursts. Measured Ruin stacks with Spell-tagged spenders such as Molten Ruin; high stored Power can threaten an entire Arena HP bar. Sword-tagged Obsidian Drill does not receive these Spell-only bonuses.
ratings.rationale: Power spending, first-spell amplification and next-turn refund support repeated bursts. Measured Ruin stacks with Spell-tagged spenders such as Molten Ruin; high stored Power can threaten an entire Arena HP bar. Sword-tagged Obsidian Drill does not receive these Spell-only bonuses.
ratings.watch: Rare stacked-burst engine and high Power requirement; assess time to assemble and counterpressure before treating S ceiling as universal S reliability.
ratings.pacing: Rare stacked-burst engine and high Power requirement; assess time to assemble and counterpressure before treating S ceiling as universal S reliability.

ratings.name: Shatterer
ratings.scaling: Permanent Fracture raises later Shatter damage. Two Fault Lines copies multiply generation; the first-six limit per copy still grants large output and later plays continue adding Fracture.
ratings.rationale: Permanent Fracture raises later Shatter damage. Two Fault Lines copies multiply generation; the first-six limit per copy still grants large output and later plays continue adding Fracture.
ratings.watch: Likely long-fight outlier; escalating proc count and escalating proc damage multiply together.
ratings.pacing: Likely long-fight outlier; escalating proc count and escalating proc damage multiply together.

ratings.name: Bonelord
ratings.scaling: Raise 2 plus another Raise 2 adds four HP across the board per turn, not four to every Thrall. Marrow improves attacks; Off the Leash converts living Thrall HP into damage. Disruption is the reliability problem.
ratings.rationale: Raise 2 plus another Raise 2 adds four HP across the board per turn, not four to every Thrall. Marrow improves attacks; Off the Leash converts living Thrall HP into damage. Disruption is the reliability problem.
ratings.watch: Tiny early Thralls and Command access; preserved armies scale much better than repeatedly cleared ones.
ratings.pacing: Tiny early Thralls and Command access; preserved armies scale much better than repeatedly cleared ones.

ratings.name: Fateweaver
ratings.scaling: Fate application scales with target max HP and accumulates alongside ordinary damage. Random targeting, cleanse and enemy companion diversion limit reliability.
ratings.rationale: Fate application scales with target max HP and accumulates alongside ordinary damage. Random targeting, cleanse and enemy companion diversion limit reliability.
ratings.watch: Percentage execution pressure is not diluted by increasing Arena HP.
ratings.pacing: Percentage execution pressure is not diluted by increasing Arena HP.

ratings.name: Soulreaper
ratings.scaling: Up to six Harvest per owner-round permanently increases Reap; Grave Chill independently adds Fate for every genuine Consume without that limit. The same engine supplies Barrier, damage and execution pressure.
ratings.rationale: Up to six Harvest per owner-round permanently increases Reap; Grave Chill independently adds Fate for every genuine Consume without that limit. The same engine supplies Barrier, damage and execution pressure.
ratings.watch: Repeated Consume engines can threaten lethal well before the intended band even at current 6x HP.
ratings.pacing: Repeated Consume engines can threaten lethal well before the intended band even at current 6x HP.

ratings.name: Brewmaster
ratings.recovery: Good once paid growth is established
ratings.scaling: Five actual Hangover payments build permanent 5%-max-HP healing and 10 Barrier each end turn. Once established it no longer requires new payments; that sustain is much larger in Arena than Campaign.
ratings.rationale: Five actual Hangover payments build permanent 5%-max-HP healing and 10 Barrier each end turn. Once established it no longer requires new payments; that sustain is much larger in Arena than Campaign.
ratings.watch: Stall/timeout advantage; gross healing is not net after Hangover or overheal.
ratings.pacing: Stall/timeout advantage; gross healing is not net after Hangover or overheal.

ratings.name: Gunslinger
ratings.recovery: Good; weapon copies grow each turn
ratings.scaling: Starting Precision plus two each own turn continues growing all Old Twelve Gauge copies. Lone-target bonus and Clutch improve output; access to the gun still depends on drawing it after play.
ratings.rationale: Starting Precision plus two each own turn continues growing all Old Twelve Gauge copies. Lone-target bonus and Clutch improve output; access to the gun still depends on drawing it after play.
ratings.watch: Reliable damage growth but survival, gun access and Hangover costs must be counted.
ratings.pacing: Reliable damage growth but survival, gun access and Hangover costs must be counted.

ratings.name: Deathwish
ratings.recovery: Limited; one rescue buys a brief window
ratings.scaling: Clutch plus a capped low-HP ramp improves attack damage. The once-fight hostile-lethal rescue is not immunity; follow-up hits, Fate and self-payment remain threats.
ratings.rationale: Clutch plus a capped low-HP ramp improves attack damage. The once-fight hostile-lethal rescue is not immunity; follow-up hits, Fate and self-payment remain threats.
ratings.watch: Low-HP plans are fragile against multi-hit, Fate and growing long-fight bursts.
ratings.pacing: Low-HP plans are fragile against multi-hit, Fate and growing long-fight bursts.

corrections: New horizon: prior extended grades were turns 6-10, not evidence of turns 10-15 parity. Old snapshots remain unchanged. Overall changes are reassessments of unchanged combat rules, not newly implemented buffs/nerfs.

Opening, extended and Campaign estimates retain 0.195.0 values except Golemancer Campaign IV-X and XVII-XX, A- to A. These are separate axes; a carried short-fight grade can differ from the new overall estimate.

Golemancer has base Engineer +1 plus Ascendancy +3 HP per companion per start, plus all healing/card growth. 160 HP is plausible but not a measured average. Heavy Hitter/Crankshaft use max HP, Meltdown/Strip for Parts current HP; no flat minion HP cap or automatic Golemancer buff recommended.
Paladin retention converges under constant Barrier generation. Bloodletter extra ticks also consume stacks. Totems cannot be attacked like minions. Bonelord Raise growth is shared across the board.
Full Trick growth belongs to every Trickster Ascendancy. Rogue Rush of Blood+ and neutral Forebear Gift provide zero-cost two-Mana/two-draw examples; do not misattribute them to the Trickster pool.
Arena 20-minute game clock implemented by explicit user request; 75-second turns unchanged. This does not guarantee ten rounds when players use all their turn time.
No simulations, measured win rates, confirmed turn-length results or post-proposal A-tier claims. Detailed proposals and Campaign risks remain pending review.
